title: What is the word of the year 2026? Maxxing, mogging and human
answer: There isn't just one. So far in 2026, Dictionary.com picked "maxxing" (late October), Collins picked "mogging" (Nov. 3) and Cambridge picked "human" (Nov. 18). Oxford and Merriam-Webster usually announce their choices later, in late November or December.
body:
Every big dictionary chooses its own word of the year, so the answer depends on whom you ask. Two of 2026's picks come straight from online slang. Dictionary.com chose "maxxing," short for maximizing: pushing something as far as it can go, usually tacked onto another word, as in "I'm sleepmaxxing this weekend." Its shortlist also included "affordability," "data center," "odyssey" and "unc." Collins chose "mogging," which means outshining someone, often used jokingly when a friend gets upstaged: "His costume completely mogged mine." Collins said use of the word rose about 210% this year.

Cambridge went the other way. On Nov. 18 it named "human," saying the choice reflects how much people now compare themselves with AI, from worries about jobs to labels like "human-made." Its shortlist included "agent" (an AI system that acts on its own), "wholesome" and "dusking," which means watching daylight fade as a way to relax. Cambridge also said it added "aura farming" and "looksmaxxing" to its dictionary this year.

Why is everyone talking about it now? Cambridge's announcement landed on Nov. 18, and the slang picks keep circulating because many adults first meet words like "maxxing" and "mogging" in these headlines. Last year's picks showed the same pattern: Dictionary.com chose "6-7," Cambridge chose "parasocial" and Oxford chose "rage bait."

For parents and teachers: both slang winners are mostly harmless jokes today, but they grew out of online "looksmaxxing" communities focused on appearance and ranking people's looks. If a child uses them a lot, it's worth a calm question about what videos they're watching. Our explainer on "maxxing" is at https://trendrundown.com/x/what-does-maxxing-mean.
in_the_news: Cambridge Dictionary named "human" its 2026 word of the year on Nov. 18, joining Dictionary.com's "maxxing" and Collins' "mogging."

faq.q: What is Oxford's word of the year for 2026?
faq.a: Oxford had not announced it as of Nov. 19, 2026. In 2025, Oxford announced "rage bait" in early December.
To outshine or upstage someone. Collins says young people often use it playfully, for example when one friend's outfit beats another's.
Cambridge said people increasingly define "human" in contrast with machines and AI, and words like "human-made" became more common.

faq.q: What was the word of the year in 2025?
faq.a: Dictionary.com chose "6-7," Cambridge chose "parasocial" and Oxford chose "rage bait."
